first.rationale: The two symptoms that are actually degrading (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same funnel stage, and two independent inherited records (memory_86 on shortening onboarding, memory_31 on cutting signup fields) converge on onboarding/signup simplification producing durable activation lift. That convergence is the strongest evidence base I have, and the intervention improves the quality of accounts that enter rather than just the count. I am verifying memory_86 because it is the record I intend to act on and I should not commit a slot to a claim I have only seen in summary form. I am verifying memory_73 because promotional pricing is the emotionally obvious answer to a competitor's entry pricing and it is precisely the memory that carries a self-flagged defect: the readout pooled two cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, so its 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' may be an artifact of the pooling rather than a real effect. Before I let competitive pressure push me into discount matching, I want the original record. Downstream value risk is real and is why I am not defaulting to promotional_pricing: discounting to defend price-sensitive SMB accounts tends to buy exactly the accounts with the worst retention and lowest expansion, which inflates near-term acquisition while degrading sustainable long-term qualified revenue -- the stated objective. It also anchors price expectations and is hard to unwind. Referral incentives (memory_57) work on established customers and do nothing for a broken top-of-funnel; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is credible but addresses a segment that is not the one deteriorating. Activation messaging (memory_91) is my fallback and would pair well later. Important caveats I am carrying forward rather than suppressing: all of these memories are 15-64 days old and were established under pre-competitor market conditions, so the mechanism that made onboarding simplification work may itself be what has decayed; the observed declines could also be a mix shift caused by the competitor skimming off the accounts that used to activate easily, in which case a funnel fix will underperform. For that reason I want a standard experiment with a proper holdout and a read on retained/qualified revenue, not just completion and first-week activation, rather than a broad rollout on inherited confidence.
